text.p: Shares in two junior Canadian mining companies soared Friday after Francisco Gold Corp released what it described as "excellent" assay results for its El Sauzal gold property in Mexico.
Francisco stock climbed 12.50 to 31 on turnover of 917,000 shares on the Vancouver Stock Exchange.

Queenstake Resources Ltd shares were the most heavily traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange, rising 1.04 to 3.54. Queenstake's Yecorato 51 property is competely surrounded by Francisco's El Sauzal in Chihuahua, Mexico.

Francisco said in a press release that phase two diamond drilling of 15 holes on its property confirmed "the existence of a world class, mineable oxide orebody in Mexico which is of unusually high grade for this type of epithermal gold deposit."

It made a preliminary geological resource estimate of 3.2 million ounces of gold at an average grade of 3.8 grams per tonne gold. Francisco officials were not available to comment further on the news release.
But analysts said the data were highly promising. "These results are pretty spectacular," said one mining analyst.
Francisco previously estimated the resource at more than two million ounces, analysts said.
Queenstake spokesman Ryan Fralic said his company believed the rise in its stock price reflected investor optimism sparked by the Francisco news.

Yecorato 51 was staked on behalf of Vulcan Gold, a Mexican company owned 60 percent by Queenstake and 40 percent by Alamos Minerals Corp. Alamos shares jumped 1.35 to 2.50 on the Vancouver Stock Exchange.
In a news release earlier this month, Queenstake said Francisco's El Sauzal "appears to be similar in geology and size to Barrick Gold Corp's Pierina project in Peru."
Barrick acquired Pierina through a C$1.1 billion takeover of Arequipa Resources Ltd last year.
